title: Open Values Format Registry
description: The list of every Open Values file format, one entry each: what the format is for, where its schema is, which files and code write it, which code reads it, and which checks enforce it. The project keeps it by hand at app/data/standard/registry.json; the standard audit and the spec pages on openvaluesstandard.org read it.

format.description: Always "open-values-format-registry". Tells a reader which Open Values format this is.

version.description: The version of the registry format this file follows, as a semantic version such as "0.1.0".

standard.description: Always "open-values-standard", the standard this registry belongs to.

standardVersion.description: The version of the Open Values Standard the registry describes, as a semantic version such as "1.0.0-draft.1".

updated.description: The date the registry was last changed, as YYYY-MM-DD.

entries.description: One entry per file format. At least one.

mode.description: How the standard audit recognises a file of this format: "explicit-format" (the file names its format in a format field), "legacy-shape" (older files with no format field, recognised by their path and shape), "schema" (the format is a schema used inside other formats, not a file of its own), "html-jsonld" (a JSON-LD block inside an HTML page), or "test-fixture".

format.description: For explicit-format files, the value the file's format field must hold, such as "open-values-lens".

pathPattern.description: Where files of this format live in the repository, as a path that may use "*", such as "content/lenses/*.json".

pathPatterns.description: Several such paths, when files of this format live in more than one place. No path may repeat.

notes.description: A sentence on how files of this format are recognised, when the mode alone does not say, such as "Existing lenses are identified by path plus meta/criteria/products shape."

acceptsLegacyVersion.description: True when older files of this format, written before the current version rules, are still accepted. The notes field says what is accepted.

acceptsBareVersion.description: True when files may declare a short version such as "0.1" instead of a full semantic version. The standard audit requires this for any entry whose declaredVersion is a short version.

breakingChangePolicy.description: A sentence on how a change that breaks existing files would be handled. No entry uses it yet.

migration.description: A sentence on how to move older files to the current version. No entry uses it yet.

notes.description: A sentence on what older or unusual files remain valid, such as "Sparse map scores and explicit null unknowns remain valid."

id.description: The format's name, such as "open-values-lens". Files of explicit-format formats carry it in their format field.

version.description: The current version of the format, as a semantic version such as "0.1.0".

declaredVersion.description: The version string files of this format actually carry, which may differ from version: a short version such as "0.1" (allowed only with acceptsBareVersion), or "none" for legacy-shape files that carry no version.

status.description: How settled the format is: stable (a breaking change needs a new version), draft (may still change), experimental, dev-contract (used while building the sites, not meant for other apps), or legacy.

kind.description: What sort of file it is: source (someone writes and keeps it), generated (a build step makes it from other files), fixture (test data), distribution (published for others to download), or internal (a shape used inside other formats, not a file on its own).

purpose.description: One sentence saying what the format is for.

marker.description: How the standard audit finds and recognises files of this format.

schema.description: The repository path of the format's JSON Schema, such as "app/data/standard/schemas/lens.schema.json", or null when there is none.

schemaNote.description: Why the format has no schema, or what checks the schema leaves to an audit. Required when schema is null.

sourceOfTruth.description: The files that define the format or hold its authored data, such as docs or the hand-edited source file.

generatedOutputs.description: The files a build step makes from this format, if any.

builders.description: The scripts that write files of this format, such as "pipeline/build_map.js".

audits.description: The commands or scripts that check files of this format, such as "npm run audit:standard".

ownerLane.description: Who maintains the format: data-lane (the data and pipeline work), app-lane (hand-edited app code), generated (only ever written by a builder), external (defined outside this repository), or shared.

runtimeConsumers.description: The code or pages that read files of this format, such as "app/homelens.js", or a short name for a planned reader.

compatibility.description: Which older or unusual files of this format are still accepted.

dependencies.description: The ids of other formats this one is built from, such as "open-values-source". Each must be an id in this registry.

formerNames.description: Names this format was published under before, which a reader treats as the same format. For example, the Hearth's position file was briefly named hearth-position.
